t: A loose union of princes, bishops and free cities in central Europe, under an elected emperor from 962 to 1806.
Its fragmentation let the Reformation survive and produced religious settlements that shaped the modern idea of state sovereignty.
Napoleon's Confederation of the Rhine made the title meaningless, and Francis II quietly dissolved the empire in 1806.
dyk: The empire had no standing army for most of its history; its military strength depended on contingents the princes sent only when politically willing.
ev: Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor in Rome on Christmas Day
Otto I is crowned emperor by Pope John XII, the empire's functional founding
The Lombard League defeats Frederick Barbarossa at Legnano
Charles IV's Golden Bull fixes the election of the emperor by seven electors
Martin Luther launches the Reformation at Wittenberg
The Peace of Augsburg lets rulers choose Catholicism or Lutheranism for their lands
The Peace of Westphalia ends the Thirty Years' War and lets princes make foreign alliances
Francis II abdicates and declares the Holy Roman Empire dissolved
